questions.question: A told B, "The Girl I met yesterday was the youngest daughter of the brother-in-law of my mother". How is the girl related to A?
questions.questionHtml: A told B, "The Girl I met yesterday was the youngest daughter of the brother-in-law of my mother". How is the girl related to A?
questions.solution:
Preparing the family tree using the following symbols,

Given:

A told B, "The Girl I met yesterday was the youngest daughter of the brother-in-law of my mother"

We can draw the following Family Tree from the information given above:

Hence, the girl is the "Cousin" of A.

Here is a detailed explanation:

A's mother's brother-in-law is A's uncle.
The youngest daughter of A's uncle is A's cousin.
Another way to think about it is to draw a family tree:

Grandfather
|
Grandmother
|
Father   Mother
|
A       Uncle
|
        Cousin


In this family tree, A and the girl are cousins because they have the same grandfather.

Here is an example of how the statement "The Girl I met yesterday was the youngest daughter of the brother-in-law of my mother" could be used in a conversation:

  • A: I met this really nice girl yesterday.
  • B: Oh? Who was she?
  • A: She was the youngest daughter of my uncle.
  • B: That's cool. How is she related to you?
  • A: Well, my uncle is my mother's brother-in-law, so the girl is my cousin.
  • B: Oh, okay. That makes sense.
